config.doc:
MH Agent 路径配置 — 同时支持开发模式和桌面打包模式。

桌面打包模式检测：环境变量 MH_DESKTOP=1 或 desktop/runtime/ 目录存在。
打包后目录结构：
    install_dir/
    ├── resources/app/          ← Electron asar 解压后的应用目录
    │   ├── main.js
    │   ├── backend/            ← Python 后端
    │   ├── dist/               ← 前端构建产物
    │   ├── tools/              ← 工具目录
    │   └── templates/          ← 模板目录
    │   （正式包不含 skills/；受保护 Skill 从签名 Capsule 获取）
    ├── runtime/
    │   ├── python/             ← 内嵌 Python
    │   ├── node/               ← 内嵌 Node.js + Claude CLI
    │   └── texlive/            ← 内嵌 TinyTeX
    └── MHAgent.exe

用户数据目录（%APPDATA%/MHAgent/）：
    ├── db/aris.db
    └── workspaces/

methods.name: __init__
methods.doc:
Create a new model by parsing and validating input data from keyword arguments.

Raises [`ValidationError`][pydantic_core.ValidationError] if the input data cannot be
validated to form a valid model.

`self` is explicitly positional-only to allow `self` as a field name.

methods.name: _setattr_handler
methods.sig: (self, name: 'str', value: 'Any') -> 'Callable[[BaseModel, str, Any], None] | None'
methods.doc:
Get a handler for setting an attribute on the model instance.

Returns:
    A handler for setting an attribute on the model instance. Used for memoization of the handler.
    Memoizing the handlers leads to a dramatic performance improvement in `__setattr__`
    Returns `None` when memoization is not safe, then the attribute is set directly.

methods.doc:
Returns a copy of the model.

!!! warning "Deprecated"
    This method is now deprecated; use `model_copy` instead.

If you need `include` or `exclude`, use:

```python {test="skip" lint="skip"}
data = self.model_dump(include=include, exclude=exclude, round_trip=True)
data = {**data, **(update or {})}
copied = self.model_validate(data)
```

Args:
    include: Optional set or mapping specifying which fields to include in the copied model.
    exclude: Optional set or mapping specifying which fields to exclude in the copied model.
    update: Optional dictionary of field-value pairs to override field values in the copied model.
    deep: If True, the values of fields that are Pydantic models will be deep-copied.

Returns:
    A copy of the model with included, excluded and updated fields as specified.

A decorator exposing the decorated class method as a property, with a warning on instance access.

This decorator takes a class method defined on the `BaseModel` class and transforms it into
an attribute. The attribute can be accessed on both the class and instances of the class. If accessed
via an instance, a deprecation warning is emitted stating that instance access will be removed in V3.

methods.name: model_construct
methods.doc:
Creates a new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Creates a new model setting `__dict__` and `__pydantic_fields_set__` from trusted or pre-validated data.
Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed.

!!! note
    `model_construct()` generally respects the `model_config.extra` setting on the provided model.
    That is, if `model_config.extra == 'allow'`, then all extra passed values are added to the model instance's `__dict__`
    and `__pydantic_extra__` fields. If `model_config.extra == 'ignore'` (the default), then all extra passed values are ignored.
    Because no validation is performed with a call to `model_construct()`, having `model_config.extra == 'forbid'` does not result in
    an error if extra values are passed, but they will be ignored.

Args:
    _fields_set: A set of field names that were originally explicitly set during instantiation. If provided,
        this is directly used for the [`model_fields_set`][pydantic.BaseModel.model_fields_set] attribute.
        Otherwise, the field names from the `values` argument will be used.
    values: Trusted or pre-validated data dictionary.

Returns:
    A new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

methods.name: model_copy
methods.sig: (self, *, update: 'Mapping[str, Any] | None' = None, deep: 'bool' = False) -> 'Self'
methods.doc:
!!! abstract "Usage Documentation"
    [`model_copy`](../concepts/models.md#model-copy)

Returns a copy of the model.

!!! note
    The underlying instance's [`__dict__`][object.__dict__] attribute is copied. This
    might have unexpected side effects if you store anything in it, on top of the model
    fields (e.g. the value of [cached properties][functools.cached_property]).

Args:
    update: Values to change/add in the new model. Note: the data is not validated
        before creating the new model. You should trust this data.
    deep: Set to `True` to make a deep copy of the model.

Returns:
    New model instance.

methods.name: model_json_schema
methods.doc:
Generates a JSON schema for a model class.

Args:
    by_alias: Whether to use attribute aliases or not.
    ref_template: The reference template.
    union_format: The format to use when combining schemas from unions together. Can be one of:

        - `'any_of'`: Use the [`anyOf`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/combining#anyOf)
        keyword to combine schemas (the default).
        - `'primitive_type_array'`: Use the [`type`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/type)
        keyword as an array of strings, containing each type of the combination. If any of the schemas is not a primitive
        type (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) or contains constraints/metadata, falls back to
        `any_of`.
    schema_generator: To override the logic used to generate the JSON schema, as a subclass of
        `GenerateJsonSchema` with your desired modifications
    mode: The mode in which to generate the schema.

Returns:
    The JSON schema for the given model class.

methods.name: model_parametrized_name
methods.doc:
Compute the class name for parametrizations of generic classes.

This method can be overridden to achieve a custom naming scheme for generic BaseModels.

Args:
    params: Tuple of types of the class. Given a generic class
        `Model` with 2 type variables and a concrete model `Model[str, int]`,
        the value `(str, int)` would be passed to `params`.

Returns:
    String representing the new class where `params` are passed to `cls` as type variables.

Raises:
    TypeError: Raised when trying to generate concrete names for non-generic models.

methods.name: model_post_init
methods.doc:
Override this method to perform additional initialization after `__init__` and `model_construct`.
This is useful if you want to do some validation that requires the entire model to be initialized.

methods.name: model_rebuild
methods.doc:
Try to rebuild the pydantic-core schema for the model.

This may be necessary when one of the annotations is a ForwardRef which could not be resolved during
the initial attempt to build the schema, and automatic rebuilding fails.

Args:
    force: Whether to force the rebuilding of the model schema, defaults to `False`.
    raise_errors: Whether to raise errors, defaults to `True`.
    _parent_namespace_depth: The depth level of the parent namespace, defaults to 2.
    _types_namespace: The types namespace, defaults to `None`.

Returns:
    Returns `None` if the schema is already "complete" and rebuilding was not required.
    If rebuilding _was_ required, returns `True` if rebuilding was successful, otherwise `False`.

methods.name: model_validate
methods.doc:
Validate a pydantic model instance.

Args:
    obj: The object to validate.
    strict: Whether to enforce types strictly.
    extra: Whether to ignore, allow, or forbid extra data during model validation.
        See the [`extra` configuration value][pydantic.ConfigDict.extra] for details.
    from_attributes: Whether to extract data from object attributes.
    context: Additional context to pass to the validator.
    by_alias: Whether to use the field's alias when validating against the provided input data.
    by_name: Whether to use the field's name when validating against the provided input data.

Raises:
    ValidationError: If the object could not be validated.

Returns:
    The validated model instance.

methods.name: model_validate_json
methods.doc:
!!! abstract "Usage Documentation"
    [JSON Parsing](../concepts/json.md#json-parsing)

Validate the given JSON data against the Pydantic model.

Args:
    json_data: The JSON data to validate.
    strict: Whether to enforce types strictly.
    extra: Whether to ignore, allow, or forbid extra data during model validation.
        See the [`extra` configuration value][pydantic.ConfigDict.extra] for details.
    context: Extra variables to pass to the validator.
    by_alias: Whether to use the field's alias when validating against the provided input data.
    by_name: Whether to use the field's name when validating against the provided input data.

Returns:
    The validated Pydantic model.

Raises:
    ValidationError: If `json_data` is not a JSON string or the object could not be validated.

methods.name: model_validate_strings
methods.doc:
Validate the given object with string data against the Pydantic model.

Args:
    obj: The object containing string data to validate.
    strict: Whether to enforce types strictly.
    extra: Whether to ignore, allow, or forbid extra data during model validation.
        See the [`extra` configuration value][pydantic.ConfigDict.extra] for details.
    context: Extra variables to pass to the validator.
    by_alias: Whether to use the field's alias when validating against the provided input data.
    by_name: Whether to use the field's name when validating against the provided input data.

Returns:
    The validated Pydantic model.

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP TRACE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.trace("/items/{item_id}")
def trace_item(item_id: str):
    return None

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Decorate a WebSocket function.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for WebSockets](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/websockets/).

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP OPTIONS operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.options("/items/")
def get_item_options():
    return {"additions": ["Aji", "Guacamole"]}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP PATCH operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.patch("/items/")
def update_item(item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item updated in place"}

app.include_router(router)
```

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

                    show it as the response (JSON Schema).

                    `response_model` would be used to serialize that object into the
                    corresponding JSON.
                * Filtering: the JSON sent to the client will only contain the data
                    (fields) defined in the `response_model`. If you returned an object
                    that contains an attribute `password` but the `response_model` does
                    not include that field, the JSON sent to the client would not have
                    that `password`.

                    `response_model`, converting any data as necessary to generate the
                    corresponding JSON. But if the data in the object returned is not
                    valid, that would mean a violation of the contract with the client,
                    so it's an error from the API developer. So, FastAPI will raise an
                    error and return a 500 error code (Internal Server Error).

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP POST operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.post("/items/")
def create_item(item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item created"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP PUT operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.put("/items/{item_id}")
def replace_item(item_id: str, item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item replaced", "id": item_id}

app.include_router(router)
```

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
```

methods.name: model_construct
methods.doc:
Creates a new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Creates a new model setting `__dict__` and `__pydantic_fields_set__` from trusted or pre-validated data.
Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed.

!!! note
    `model_construct()` generally respects the `model_config.extra` setting on the provided model.
    That is, if `model_config.extra == 'allow'`, then all extra passed values are added to the model instance's `__dict__`
    and `__pydantic_extra__` fields. If `model_config.extra == 'ignore'` (the default), then all extra passed values are ignored.
    Because no validation is performed with a call to `model_construct()`, having `model_config.extra == 'forbid'` does not result in
    an error if extra values are passed, but they will be ignored.

Args:
    _fields_set: A set of field names that were originally explicitly set during instantiation. If provided,
        this is directly used for the [`model_fields_set`][pydantic.BaseModel.model_fields_set] attribute.
        Otherwise, the field names from the `values` argument will be used.
    values: Trusted or pre-validated data dictionary.

Returns:
    A new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

errors.name: HTTPException
errors.doc:
An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client.

This is for client errors, invalid authentication, invalid data, etc. Not for server
errors in your code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Handling Errors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

items = {"foo": "The Foo Wrestlers"}


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item": items[item_id]}
```

`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
```

```python
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP PATCH operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.patch("/items/")
def update_item(item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item updated in place"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP POST operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.post("/items/")
def create_item(item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item created"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP PUT operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.put("/items/{item_id}")
def replace_item(item_id: str, item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item replaced", "id": item_id}

app.include_router(router)
```

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:

        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.name: model_construct
methods.doc:
Creates a new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Creates a new model setting `__dict__` and `__pydantic_fields_set__` from trusted or pre-validated data.
Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed.

!!! note
    `model_construct()` generally respects the `model_config.extra` setting on the provided model.
    That is, if `model_config.extra == 'allow'`, then all extra passed values are added to the model instance's `__dict__`
    and `__pydantic_extra__` fields. If `model_config.extra == 'ignore'` (the default), then all extra passed values are ignored.
    Because no validation is performed with a call to `model_construct()`, having `model_config.extra == 'forbid'` does not result in
    an error if extra values are passed, but they will be ignored.

Args:
    _fields_set: A set of field names that were originally explicitly set during instantiation. If provided,
        this is directly used for the [`model_fields_set`][pydantic.BaseModel.model_fields_set] attribute.
        Otherwise, the field names from the `values` argument will be used.
    values: Trusted or pre-validated data dictionary.

Returns:
    A new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

classes.name: UploadFile
classes.doc:
A file uploaded in a request.

Define it as a *path operation function* (or dependency) parameter.

If you are using a regular `def` function, you can use the `upload_file.file`
attribute to access the raw standard Python file (blocking, not async), useful and
needed for non-async code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Request Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/request-files/).

## Example

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, File, UploadFile

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/files/")
async def create_file(file: Annotated[bytes, File()]):
    return {"file_size": len(file)}


@app.post("/uploadfile/")
async def create_upload_file(file: UploadFile):
    return {"filename": file.filename}
```

functions.doc:
判定工作区内某相对路径是否为"非交付物噪音"(编译垃圾/依赖/构建/内部状态)。
list_artifacts(展示) 与 export_workspace(下载 zip) 共用。

⛔ for_export 区分两种口径：
  - 展示(for_export=False)：追求干净——隐藏 paper/figures 编译拷贝、字体、figures 下内部数据，避免重复/臃肿。
  - 导出(for_export=True)：追求可复现——这些"展示噪音"其实是**本地重新编译必需**的
    (paper/figures 供 \includegraphics、中文字体供 xelatex)，必须保留在 zip 里，否则用户拿回去编不出来。
  两种口径都过滤的是**真·throwaway**(_tmp_smoke 探活垃圾、0 字节 _PASSED 标记、编译中间产物)。

errors.name: HTTPException
errors.doc:
An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client.

This is for client errors, invalid authentication, invalid data, etc. Not for server
errors in your code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Handling Errors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

items = {"foo": "The Foo Wrestlers"}


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item": items[item_id]}
```

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

Decorate a WebSocket function.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for WebSockets](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/websockets/).

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.name: model_construct
methods.doc:
Creates a new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Creates a new model setting `__dict__` and `__pydantic_fields_set__` from trusted or pre-validated data.
Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed.

!!! note
    `model_construct()` generally respects the `model_config.extra` setting on the provided model.
    That is, if `model_config.extra == 'allow'`, then all extra passed values are added to the model instance's `__dict__`
    and `__pydantic_extra__` fields. If `model_config.extra == 'ignore'` (the default), then all extra passed values are ignored.
    Because no validation is performed with a call to `model_construct()`, having `model_config.extra == 'forbid'` does not result in
    an error if extra values are passed, but they will be ignored.

Args:
    _fields_set: A set of field names that were originally explicitly set during instantiation. If provided,
        this is directly used for the [`model_fields_set`][pydantic.BaseModel.model_fields_set] attribute.
        Otherwise, the field names from the `values` argument will be used.
    values: Trusted or pre-validated data dictionary.

Returns:
    A new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Generates a JSON schema for a model class.

Args:

    ref_template: The reference template.
    union_format: The format to use when combining schemas from unions together. Can be one of:

        - `'any_of'`: Use the [`anyOf`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/combining#anyOf)
        keyword to combine schemas (the default).
        - `'primitive_type_array'`: Use the [`type`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/type)
        keyword as an array of strings, containing each type of the combination. If any of the schemas is not a primitive
        type (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) or contains constraints/metadata, falls back to
        `any_of`.

This method can be overridden to achieve a custom naming scheme for generic BaseModels.

Args:

        `Model` with 2 type variables and a concrete model `Model[str, int]`,
        the value `(str, int)` would be passed to `params`.

Try to rebuild the pydantic-core schema for the model.

This may be necessary when one of the annotations is a ForwardRef which could not be resolved during
the initial attempt to build the schema, and automatic rebuilding fails.

Args:
    force: Whether to force the rebuilding of the model schema, defaults to `False`.
    raise_errors: Whether to raise errors, defaults to `True`.
    _parent_namespace_depth: The depth level of the parent namespace, defaults to 2.
    _types_namespace: The types namespace, defaults to `None`.

Returns:

    If rebuilding _was_ required, returns `True` if rebuilding was successful, otherwise `False`.

classes.name: UploadFile
classes.doc:
A file uploaded in a request.

Define it as a *path operation function* (or dependency) parameter.

If you are using a regular `def` function, you can use the `upload_file.file`
attribute to access the raw standard Python file (blocking, not async), useful and
needed for non-async code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Request Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/request-files/).

## Example

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, File, UploadFile

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/files/")
async def create_file(file: Annotated[bytes, File()]):
    return {"file_size": len(file)}


@app.post("/uploadfile/")
async def create_upload_file(file: UploadFile):
    return {"filename": file.filename}
```
classes.sig: (file: 'BinaryIO', *, size: 'int | None' = None, filename: 'str | None' = None, headers: 'Headers | None' = None) -> 'None'

methods.doc:
Close the file.

To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.

methods.sig: (self, size: typing.Annotated[int, Doc('\n                The number of bytes to read from the file.\n                ')] = -1) -> bytes
methods.doc:
Read some bytes from the file.

To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.

methods.sig: (self, offset: typing.Annotated[int, Doc('\n                The position in bytes to seek to in the file.\n                ')]) -> None
methods.doc:
Move to a position in the file.

Any next read or write will be done from that position.

To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.

methods.doc:
Write some bytes to the file.

You normally wouldn't use this from a file you read in a request.

To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.

functions.name: _active_runtime_context
functions.doc:
Return the same live task truth that drives proposal cards.

The long-lived assistant cannot observe frontend card transitions by itself.
Without this bounded snapshot it may keep repeating the proposal-time phrase
"等待确认" after the user has already confirmed and the task is running.
Only allow-listed, user-visible fields are included; raw commands, private
paths, model streams and Skill contents never enter this context.

functions.name: _complete_turn_text
functions.doc: Persist all user constraints; the 500-character focus is only a label.

functions.name: _confirmed_version_map
functions.doc:
Persisted cards need validation too (older imports need not be typed).

A legacy SQL NULL denotes no explicit inputs. JSON null/list/corruption
does not: silently treating it as {} loses the user's confirmed dependency.

functions.name: _context_recovery_input
_open_session_inner
functions.doc:
打开（或复用）对话会话。前端进入工作台时调。

⛔ 这里会真起一个 claude 进程 + 跑一轮可计费探针。
   所以前端只在进入页面时调一次，不要放在轮询里。

functions.name: _pending_context
functions.doc:
Return a bounded recent-task memory plus ids not yet acknowledged.

Unconsumed events guarantee delivery after a task finishes.  The latest
events are also replayed on later turns so CLI resume/context compaction
cannot make the assistant forget a modification that is still relevant.
Raw diffs are deliberately excluded; the review endpoint remains their
single source of truth.

functions.name: _pending_fork_topics
functions.doc: Return unresolved AI-made choices that must be surfaced before downstream work.

functions.name: _project_brief
functions.doc: Return the stable public shape, tolerating older/malformed databases.

functions.name: _public_diff_metadata
functions.doc: Return compact review metadata, upgrading pre-V2 stored diffs lazily.

functions.name: _public_messages
functions.doc: Use the same bounded display metadata in conversation and task history.

functions.name: _recent_conversation_context
functions.doc: Replay a tiny transcript only when the underlying CLI process rotates.

functions.name: _require_chat_mode
functions.doc: 服务端模式闸：不能只相信前端是否显示协同页面。

functions.name: _say_impl
functions.doc:
发一句话给主会话。

主会话可能：① 直接回答 ② 调 propose_skill 建提议（走 chat_internal）。
提议卡片通过 WS 推给前端，本接口只返回助手的文字回复。

functions.name: _send_serialized
functions.sig: (wf_id: 'str', sess, model_text: 'str', *, mode: 'str', focus_target: 'str', turn_id: 'str', recovery_text: 'Optional[str]' = None) -> 'dict'
functions.doc: 把“本轮范围状态 + 主会话发送”放进同一把锁，防并发串台。

functions.name: accept_existing_stage
functions.doc: User-triggered local acceptance, no model, no paper rewrite, no next run.

functions.name: add_decision
functions.doc:
手工记一条决定。

⛔ 为什么必须有这个入口：自动识别（chat_decisions.detect_rejection）
   必然有漏 ——「别用遗传算法」能认，「GA 不合适」「那套方法风险大」未必。
   没有手工兜底就又是"看起来在记、实际漏了"，比没有这功能更坑人。

functions.name: build_workspace_evidence
functions.doc: Build a bounded evidence block without making a model/tool call.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc:
取消提议或正在跑的任务。

⛔ 三种状态三种处理：
   proposed —— 直接改库（还没进队列）
   queued   —— 改库，消费循环出队时会跳过（不碰进程）
   running  —— 必须杀进程

functions.name: choose_fork
functions.doc:
选定一个岔路口。

⛔ 选完【立刻写进决定清单】—— 这是整个岔路口功能的意义所在：
   不写进去的话，你的选择只停留在界面上，下一步 skill 根本不知道。

functions.name: close_session
functions.doc: 关闭会话（前端离开工作台、或用户主动结束）。

functions.name: confirm
functions.doc:
用户点「跑」。这是唯一能让 skill 真正执行的入口。

⛔ 三道闸按顺序：
   ① 消息必须是 proposed 状态（不能重复确认、不能确认已取消的）
   ② 依赖必须齐（出队时还会再查一次，因为排队期间可能变）
   ③ 上游指纹必须没变 —— 你收到卡片去吃饭，回来点「跑」，
      这期间上游可能被改过，卡片上写的"基于 X@a1b2"已不成立

Never release workspace ownership while a cancelled worker still writes.

Synchronous checkers have their own finite subprocess timeouts. Cancellation
waits for their safe completion without blocking API/event-loop responses.

WebSocket delivery is only a low-latency hint.  This endpoint is the

⛔ 不打断正在跑的那条 —— 那会损坏工作区（两个进程写同一批文件）。

队列面板：正在跑的 + 排队中的，带每条的 skill 和预计耗时。

⛔ 正在跑的那条已经不在队列里了（消费循环 get 出来了），要单独取。

撤销不是“强制覆盖旧文件”：只有文件仍等于该 patch 的提交版本时才允许，
后续任何人工或 AI 修改都会触发冲突并拒绝撤销。

errors.name: HTTPException
errors.doc:
An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client.

This is for client errors, invalid authentication, invalid data, etc. Not for server
errors in your code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Handling Errors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

items = {"foo": "The Foo Wrestlers"}


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item": items[item_id]}
```

routers.chat_internal.doc:
给 MCP server 子进程用的窄权限接口。

⛔ 为什么单独一个 router、单独一套鉴权：
   main.py 的注释写着「不把 Electron 控制 token 或 License Lease 交给子进程」。
   MCP server 是 Claude CLI 派生的子进程，要回调后端建提议记录 —— 但绝不能给它
   MODEX_CONTROL_TOKEN，那等于把整个后端 API 的钥匙（含 /api/settings 里的真实
   API Key）交出去。所以走独立短票 + 路径白名单，照 /v1/messages 的 CLI 代理模式。

⛔ 本文件下的接口有三条铁律，破了任意一条就等于开后门：
   1. 只暴露提议、依赖、状态和受控公开产物读取，不提供任意路径文件工具
   2. 任何响应都不含配置、密钥、settings 内容
   3. 每个接口第一行就 authorize()，同时核 session_id 和 workflow_id

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP PATCH operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.patch("/items/")
def update_item(item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item updated in place"}

app.include_router(router)
```

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.name: model_construct
methods.doc:
Creates a new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Creates a new model setting `__dict__` and `__pydantic_fields_set__` from trusted or pre-validated data.
Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed.

!!! note
    `model_construct()` generally respects the `model_config.extra` setting on the provided model.
    That is, if `model_config.extra == 'allow'`, then all extra passed values are added to the model instance's `__dict__`
    and `__pydantic_extra__` fields. If `model_config.extra == 'ignore'` (the default), then all extra passed values are ignored.
    Because no validation is performed with a call to `model_construct()`, having `model_config.extra == 'forbid'` does not result in
    an error if extra values are passed, but they will be ignored.

Args:
    _fields_set: A set of field names that were originally explicitly set during instantiation. If provided,
        this is directly used for the [`model_fields_set`][pydantic.BaseModel.model_fields_set] attribute.
        Otherwise, the field names from the `values` argument will be used.
    values: Trusted or pre-validated data dictionary.

Returns:
    A new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

        type (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) or contains constraints/metadata, falls back to
        `any_of`.
    schema_generator: To override the logic used to generate the JSON schema, as a subclass of
        `GenerateJsonSchema` with your desired modifications
    mode: The mode in which to generate the schema.

Returns:
    The JSON schema for the given model class.

methods.name: model_parametrized_name
methods.doc:
Compute the class name for parametrizations of generic classes.

This method can be overridden to achieve a custom naming scheme for generic BaseModels.

Args:
    params: Tuple of types of the class. Given a generic class
        `Model` with 2 type variables and a concrete model `Model[str, int]`,
        the value `(str, int)` would be passed to `params`.

Returns:
    String representing the new class where `params` are passed to `cls` as type variables.

Raises:
    TypeError: Raised when trying to generate concrete names for non-generic models.

methods.name: model_post_init
methods.doc:
Override this method to perform additional initialization after `__init__` and `model_construct`.
This is useful if you want to do some validation that requires the entire model to be initialized.

methods.name: model_rebuild
methods.doc:
Try to rebuild the pydantic-core schema for the model.

This may be necessary when one of the annotations is a ForwardRef which could not be resolved during
the initial attempt to build the schema, and automatic rebuilding fails.

Args:
    force: Whether to force the rebuilding of the model schema, defaults to `False`.
    raise_errors: Whether to raise errors, defaults to `True`.
    _parent_namespace_depth: The depth level of the parent namespace, defaults to 2.
    _types_namespace: The types namespace, defaults to `None`.

Returns:
    Returns `None` if the schema is already "complete" and rebuilding was not required.
    If rebuilding _was_ required, returns `True` if rebuilding was successful, otherwise `False`.

methods.name: model_validate
methods.doc:
Validate a pydantic model instance.

Args:
    obj: The object to validate.
    strict: Whether to enforce types strictly.
    extra: Whether to ignore, allow, or forbid extra data during model validation.
        See the [`extra` configuration value][pydantic.ConfigDict.extra] for details.
    from_attributes: Whether to extract data from object attributes.
    context: Additional context to pass to the validator.
    by_alias: Whether to use the field's alias when validating against the provided input data.
    by_name: Whether to use the field's name when validating against the provided input data.

Raises:
    ValidationError: If the object could not be validated.

Returns:
    The validated model instance.

methods.name: model_validate_json
methods.doc:
!!! abstract "Usage Documentation"

Validate the given JSON data against the Pydantic model.

Args:

functions.name: _append_existing_derived_targets
functions.doc:
Preserve the generated-output closure when a proposal is edited.

This also hardens explicitly requested focused runs where the caller listed
a generator but forgot one of its already-existing exports.

functions.name: _authorize
functions.doc:
⛔ 每个接口的第一行。同时核 session 和 workflow —— 只核 token 有效性的话，
A 工作区的 MCP server 能拿自己的合法票去操作 B 工作区。

weight=0 给只读接口（/deps、/state）：核验但不扣额度。

functions.name: _broadcast
functions.doc:
⛔ 广播失败绝不能让接口挂掉 —— 库已经写了，WS 只是通知。
前端有重连重拉 + 轮询兜底，丢一条事件不致命。

functions.name: _combined_request
functions.doc:
Keep the user's wording and the model-expanded instruction in scope.

Short contextual replies such as “全都改” are not descriptive enough on
their own.  Previously they hid the detailed instruction and caused the
backend to miss “重新导出 PDF”.

functions.name: _configured_preset_id
functions.doc: 返回配置里的预设 id，不解析也不接触 API Key。

functions.name: _eta_for
functions.doc: 预计耗时：优先用该 skill 的历史中位数，没有就用静态值。

functions.name: _generated_target_closure
functions.doc:
Build an exact, reviewable source + derived-output allowlist.

Only relationships proven from public files are admitted.  Inputs merely
read by a generator are excluded, so this does not broaden write access to
datasets or unrelated artifacts.

functions.name: _infer_patch_targets
functions.doc: Resolve a minimal existing-file allowlist; never infer directories/binaries.

functions.name: _iter_public_files
functions.doc: Stream non-symlink public files without materialising the whole tree.

functions.name: _looks_focused_request
functions.doc: 保守识别明显的局部需求，兜住主会话把“只做第一问”误报 full。

functions.name: _looks_patch_request
functions.doc: Recognise explicit requests to change an artifact that already exists.

functions.name: _normalise_validation_targets
functions.doc: 只读检查可指向 PDF/图片等非可编辑产物，但仍只能访问公开普通文件。

functions.name: _proposal_snapshot
functions.doc: 生成不含秘密的模型/强度快照，供排队后的任务稳定执行。

functions.name: _public_file
functions.doc: Resolve one readable public file without following symlinks.

functions.name: _require_chat_plan
functions.doc: 提案阶段就做模式和 V2 签名计划校验，避免展示必然执行失败的卡片。

functions.name: _upstream_fingerprint
functions.doc:
只取【上游产物】的哈希做指纹 —— 上游没变，过期结论必然不变。

⛔ 不能用全量快照做指纹：那要 83ms，跟直接算过期一样贵，缓存就没意义了。
上游集合通常只有 5-8 个（PROBLEM_ANALYSIS.md / MODELING_REPORT.md /
RESULTS.md / figures/ / paper/main.tex），算指纹是毫秒级。

functions.name: artifact_request_error
functions.doc:
Stable machine code plus legacy-compatible human detail, never HTTP 500.

No retry or authority expansion is inferred from the model's paraphrase.

functions.name: dep_fingerprint
functions.doc:
提议时上游产物的指纹。确认时比对 —— 你收到卡片去吃饭，回来点「跑」，
这期间上游可能被改过，卡片上写的"基于 X@a1b2"已不成立。

functions.name: deps
functions.doc: 主会话想在提议之前先确认能不能跑时用。

functions.name: invalidate_stale
functions.doc: 产物变更后必须调 —— 否则记忆段里写的是旧的过期结论。

functions.name: positive_action_text
functions.doc: Exclude prohibitions per clause, so a ban on plotting doesn't ban solving.

functions.name: propose
functions.doc:
MCP 工具调用它，然后【立刻返回】—— 不等执行。

⛔ MCP 是请求-响应协议，comp-code 要跑 32 分钟，客户端等不到就超时。
   所以这里只建 proposed 记录 + 广播卡片，真正执行走后端自己的队列。

functions.name: set_broadcast
functions.doc: main.py 启动时注入 ws.manager.broadcast。

functions.name: state
functions.doc:
.mh/STATE.json 的摘要。回答"某数字哪来的/为什么这么定/踩过什么坑"用。

⛔ 只返回记忆内容，不含任何配置或密钥。

errors.name: HTTPException
errors.doc:
An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client.

This is for client errors, invalid authentication, invalid data, etc. Not for server
errors in your code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Handling Errors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

items = {"foo": "The Foo Wrestlers"}


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item": items[item_id]}
```

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.options("/items/")

    return {"additions": ["Aji", "Guacamole"]}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP PATCH operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.patch("/items/")
def update_item(item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item updated in place"}

app.include_router(router)
```

Decorate a WebSocket function.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for WebSockets](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/websockets/).

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.name: model_construct
methods.doc:
Creates a new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Creates a new model setting `__dict__` and `__pydantic_fields_set__` from trusted or pre-validated data.
Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed.

!!! note
    `model_construct()` generally respects the `model_config.extra` setting on the provided model.
    That is, if `model_config.extra == 'allow'`, then all extra passed values are added to the model instance's `__dict__`
    and `__pydantic_extra__` fields. If `model_config.extra == 'ignore'` (the default), then all extra passed values are ignored.
    Because no validation is performed with a call to `model_construct()`, having `model_config.extra == 'forbid'` does not result in
    an error if extra values are passed, but they will be ignored.

Args:
    _fields_set: A set of field names that were originally explicitly set during instantiation. If provided,
        this is directly used for the [`model_fields_set`][pydantic.BaseModel.model_fields_set] attribute.
        Otherwise, the field names from the `values` argument will be used.
    values: Trusted or pre-validated data dictionary.

Returns:
    A new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Generates a JSON schema for a model class.

Args:
    by_alias: Whether to use attribute aliases or not.
    ref_template: The reference template.
    union_format: The format to use when combining schemas from unions together. Can be one of:

        - `'any_of'`: Use the [`anyOf`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/combining#anyOf)
        keyword to combine schemas (the default).
        - `'primitive_type_array'`: Use the [`type`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/type)
        keyword as an array of strings, containing each type of the combination. If any of the schemas is not a primitive
        type (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) or contains constraints/metadata, falls back to
        `any_of`.
    schema_generator: To override the logic used to generate the JSON schema, as a subclass of
        `GenerateJsonSchema` with your desired modifications

Returns:

Compute the class name for parametrizations of generic classes.

This method can be overridden to achieve a custom naming scheme for generic BaseModels.

Args:
    params: Tuple of types of the class. Given a generic class
        `Model` with 2 type variables and a concrete model `Model[str, int]`,
        the value `(str, int)` would be passed to `params`.

Returns:

Raises:
    TypeError: Raised when trying to generate concrete names for non-generic models.

methods.name: model_rebuild

Try to rebuild the pydantic-core schema for the model.

This may be necessary when one of the annotations is a ForwardRef which could not be resolved during
the initial attempt to build the schema, and automatic rebuilding fails.

Args:
    force: Whether to force the rebuilding of the model schema, defaults to `False`.
    raise_errors: Whether to raise errors, defaults to `True`.
    _parent_namespace_depth: The depth level of the parent namespace, defaults to 2.
    _types_namespace: The types namespace, defaults to `None`.

Returns:
    Returns `None` if the schema is already "complete" and rebuilding was not required.
    If rebuilding _was_ required, returns `True` if rebuilding was successful, otherwise `False`.

errors.name: HTTPException
errors.doc:
An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client.

This is for client errors, invalid authentication, invalid data, etc. Not for server
errors in your code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Handling Errors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

items = {"foo": "The Foo Wrestlers"}


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item": items[item_id]}
```

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
```

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.options("/items/")
def get_item_options():
    return {"additions": ["Aji", "Guacamole"]}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP PATCH operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.patch("/items/")
def update_item(item: Item):
    return {"message": "Item updated in place"}

app.include_router(router)
```

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

methods.sig:
(self, path: typing.Annotated[str, Doc('
                The URL path to be used for this *path operation*.

                For example, in `http://example.com/items`, the path is `/items`.
                ')], *, response_model: Annotated[Any, Doc("
                The type to use for the response.

                It could be any valid Pydantic *field* type. So, it doesn't have to
                be a Pydantic model, it could be other things, like a `list`, `dict`,
                etc.

                It will be used for:

                * Documentation: the generated OpenAPI (and the UI at `/docs`) will
                    show it as the response (JSON Schema).
                * Serialization: you could return an arbitrary object and the
                    `response_model` would be used to serialize that object into the
                    corresponding JSON.
                * Filtering: the JSON sent to the client will only contain the data
                    (fields) defined in the `response_model`. If you returned an object
                    that contains an attribute `password` but the `response_model` does
                    not include that field, the JSON sent to the client would not have
                    that `password`.
                * Validation: whatever you return will be serialized with the
                    `response_model`, converting any data as necessary to generate the
                    corresponding JSON. But if the data in the object returned is not
                    valid, that would mean a violation of the contract with the client,
                    so it's an error from the API developer. So, FastAPI will raise an

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP TRACE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.trace("/items/{item_id}")
def trace_item(item_id: str):
    return None

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Decorate a WebSocket function.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for WebSockets](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/websockets/).

**Example**

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}")

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.name: model_construct
methods.doc:
Creates a new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Creates a new model setting `__dict__` and `__pydantic_fields_set__` from trusted or pre-validated data.
Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed.

!!! note
    `model_construct()` generally respects the `model_config.extra` setting on the provided model.
    That is, if `model_config.extra == 'allow'`, then all extra passed values are added to the model instance's `__dict__`
    and `__pydantic_extra__` fields. If `model_config.extra == 'ignore'` (the default), then all extra passed values are ignored.
    Because no validation is performed with a call to `model_construct()`, having `model_config.extra == 'forbid'` does not result in
    an error if extra values are passed, but they will be ignored.

Args:
    _fields_set: A set of field names that were originally explicitly set during instantiation. If provided,
        this is directly used for the [`model_fields_set`][pydantic.BaseModel.model_fields_set] attribute.
        Otherwise, the field names from the `values` argument will be used.
    values: Trusted or pre-validated data dictionary.

Returns:
    A new instance of the `Model` class with validated data.

Returns a copy of the model.

!!! note

    might have unexpected side effects if you store anything in it, on top of the model

Args:

methods.name: model_json_schema
methods.doc:
Generates a JSON schema for a model class.

Args:
    by_alias: Whether to use attribute aliases or not.
    ref_template: The reference template.
    union_format: The format to use when combining schemas from unions together. Can be one of:

        - `'any_of'`: Use the [`anyOf`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/combining#anyOf)
        keyword to combine schemas (the default).
        - `'primitive_type_array'`: Use the [`type`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/type)
        keyword as an array of strings, containing each type of the combination. If any of the schemas is not a primitive
        type (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) or contains constraints/metadata, falls back to
        `any_of`.
    schema_generator: To override the logic used to generate the JSON schema, as a subclass of
        `GenerateJsonSchema` with your desired modifications
    mode: The mode in which to generate the schema.

Returns:
    The JSON schema for the given model class.

methods.name: model_parametrized_name
methods.doc:
Compute the class name for parametrizations of generic classes.

This method can be overridden to achieve a custom naming scheme for generic BaseModels.

Args:
    params: Tuple of types of the class. Given a generic class
        `Model` with 2 type variables and a concrete model `Model[str, int]`,
        the value `(str, int)` would be passed to `params`.

Returns:
    String representing the new class where `params` are passed to `cls` as type variables.

Raises:
    TypeError: Raised when trying to generate concrete names for non-generic models.

methods.name: model_rebuild
methods.doc:
Try to rebuild the pydantic-core schema for the model.

This may be necessary when one of the annotations is a ForwardRef which could not be resolved during
the initial attempt to build the schema, and automatic rebuilding fails.

Args:
    force: Whether to force the rebuilding of the model schema, defaults to `False`.
    raise_errors: Whether to raise errors, defaults to `True`.
    _parent_namespace_depth: The depth level of the parent namespace, defaults to 2.
    _types_namespace: The types namespace, defaults to `None`.

Returns:
    Returns `None` if the schema is already "complete" and rebuilding was not required.
    If rebuilding _was_ required, returns `True` if rebuilding was successful, otherwise `False`.

errors.name: HTTPException
errors.doc:
An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client.

This is for client errors, invalid authentication, invalid data, etc. Not for server
errors in your code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Handling Errors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

items = {"foo": "The Foo Wrestlers"}


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item": items[item_id]}
```

routers.editor.doc:
LaTeX 在线编辑器 API — 文件读写 + 编译 + AI 辅助修改

支持两种工作流模式：
- LaTeX 模式（output_format=pdf 或科研类）：编辑 .tex/.bib/.py，编译用 xelatex 输出 PDF
- Markdown/Word 模式（output_format=docx 或学术写作类）：编辑 .md/.py，导出用 docx-cn-engine 输出 .docx

模式由工作流的 template + params.output_format 自动判断。

classes.name: APIRouter
classes.doc:
`APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]


app.include_router(router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP DELETE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(item_id: str):
    return {"message": "Item deleted"}

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Serve a static frontend build as low-priority routes.

Use this for frontend tools that build static files into a directory,
such as `dist`. **FastAPI** path operations are checked first, and
the frontend files are checked only if no normal route matched.

A typical project could look like this:

```text
.
├── pyproject.toml
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
└── dist
    ├── index.html
    └── assets
        └── app.js
```

Then in `app/main.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
router.frontend("/", directory="dist")
app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Add a *path operation* using an HTTP HEAD operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.head("/items/", status_code=204)
def get_items_headers(response: Response):
    response.headers["X-Cat-Dog"] = "Alone in the world"

app.include_router(router)
```

methods.doc:
Include another `APIRouter` in the same current `APIRouter`.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
internal_router = APIRouter()
users_router = APIRouter()

@users_router.get("/users/")
def read_users():
    return [{"name": "Rick"}, {"name": "Morty"}]

internal_router.include_router(users_router)
app.include_router(internal_router)
```

Add a *path operation* using an HTTP TRACE operation.

## Example

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()

@router.trace("/items/{item_id}")
def trace_item(item_id: str):
    return None

app.include_router(router)
```
